title: Practice Exam 7
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren on and lights flashing. What must you do?
choices: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until it has passed
Continue at the same speed and stay in your lane
Speed up to get out of the area quickly
Stop immediately wherever you are, even in an intersection
questions.explanation: Yield to an approaching emergency vehicle by pulling over to the right edge of the road and stopping until it passes.

questions.question: A yellow diamond sign with a merging arrow means what?
choices: Traffic from another roadway will merge with yours; adjust speed and position
You must come to a complete stop and merge
The right lane ends and merging is prohibited
A passing lane is beginning
questions.explanation: A merge warning sign alerts you that another lane of traffic will join yours ahead, so be ready to adjust your speed to let vehicles merge smoothly.

questions.question: Why must you still be prepared to stop even when your light turns green?
choices: Cross traffic or pedestrians may still be clearing the intersection
A green light always changes back to red within two seconds
Other drivers are required to honk before entering
Green lights do not grant any right-of-way
questions.explanation: A green light gives the right-of-way only if the intersection is clear; you must yield to vehicles or pedestrians still in the intersection before proceeding.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: When parking parallel to a curb, how close to the curb must your wheels be?
choices: Within 18 inches of the curb
Within 6 inches of the curb
Within 3 feet of the curb
Within 12 inches of the curb
questions.explanation: You must park within 18 inches of the curb when parking parallel.

questions.question: A series of yellow chevron (arrow-shaped) signs along a curve tells you what?
choices: The direction the road curves and to slow down as needed
A passing lane is opening on the left
The freeway is ending ahead
You may not change lanes through the curve
questions.explanation: Chevron signs point in the direction the road bends, warning drivers to reduce speed and stay in their lane through a sharp curve.

questions.question: If you must drive through a residential area near a school, the best speed management practice is to:
choices: Drive slowly and scan between parked cars for children
Maintain the maximum legal speed
Watch only the road directly ahead
Use your high beams during the day
questions.explanation: Children can emerge suddenly from between parked cars near schools, so drive slowly and scan ahead and to the sides.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed when approaching an intersection where your view of cross traffic is blocked (a blind intersection)?
choices: 15 mph
25 mph
20 mph
10 mph
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection — one with no stop signs at any corner and a blocked view — you may not drive faster than 15 mph. Slow down and edge forward until you can see.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: You are stopped at a red light and want to turn right. When is the right turn on red permitted?
choices: After a full stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, unless a sign prohibits it
Only when a green arrow appears
Never; right turns on red are illegal in California
Without stopping, as long as no pedestrians are present
questions.explanation: In California you may turn right on a red light after stopping completely and yielding, unless a 'No Turn on Red' sign is posted.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should return to your original lane only when you can see what in your mirror?
choices: The front of the vehicle you passed
Only the roof of the vehicle you passed
The road two cars behind you
Nothing; just signal and move over immediately
questions.explanation: Do not return to your lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, ensuring you have enough room not to cut it off.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean?
choices: Do not cross them to pass, except when turning left
You may pass freely in either direction
Traffic on both sides travels the same direction
They mark a designated bicycle lane
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions, though you may cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or road.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal require?
choices: Stop and do not move in the direction of the arrow until it turns green
Stop, then turn in the direction of the arrow when clear
Slow down and proceed in the arrow's direction
Yield to oncoming traffic, then turn
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you may not move in that direction at all; you must wait. Unlike a round red light, you cannot turn on a red arrow.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: Grooming yourself, such as applying makeup or shaving, while driving is:
choices: A dangerous distraction that takes attention off the road
Safe as long as you do it at low speed
Acceptable while stopped at a red light only
Only a problem for new drivers
questions.explanation: Personal grooming takes your eyes, hands, and mind off driving and is a serious distraction. Such tasks should be done before you start driving.

questions.question: Reaction distance refers to which part of stopping?
choices: The distance the vehicle travels from when you decide to brake until you actually press the pedal
The distance traveled while the brakes slow the car to a stop
The distance it takes your eyes to spot the hazard
The distance the car coasts after the brakes are released
questions.explanation: Reaction distance is how far the vehicle travels in the time between deciding to stop and physically applying the brakes.

questions.question: Before opening your car door after parking on a street, you should:
choices: Check for approaching bicyclists and traffic, even using the far hand to look back
Open it quickly to get out fast
Rely on your side mirror only
Open it fully and wait
questions.explanation: Check over your shoulder for bicyclists and traffic before opening your door; using your far hand naturally turns your body to look back.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: You are stopped behind a school bus on a two-lane road. The bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. What must you do?
choices: Remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm folds back
Pass on the left once you check that no children are visible
Proceed slowly past the bus at no more than 10 mph
Pass on the right shoulder to avoid the children
questions.explanation: When a school bus shows flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing, because children may be crossing.

questions.question: Driving in heavy rain, fog, or snow, you should keep a following distance of at least how many seconds?
choices: Four or more seconds
Two seconds
Three seconds
One second
questions.explanation: In poor conditions like rain, fog, or snow, increase your following distance well beyond the normal three seconds — about four or more seconds.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street with parked cars on the right and an emergency vehicle approaches. What is the best action?
choices: Pull over to the nearest edge of the road and stop, whichever side is clear
Always pull to the right side only
Stop in the middle of the street
Speed up to reach the next intersection
questions.explanation: On a one-way street you may pull to the nearest curb on either side and stop so the emergency vehicle can pass.

questions.question: What does it mean when a bicyclist extends their left arm straight out to the side?
choices: The cyclist intends to turn left
The cyclist intends to turn right
The cyclist is going to stop
The cyclist is warning of road debris
questions.explanation: A bicyclist's left arm extended straight out signals a left turn, just as it does for drivers using hand signals.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: How far from a disabled-access (wheelchair) curb ramp must you avoid parking?
choices: Within 3 feet of the ramp
Within 6 feet of the ramp
Within 1 foot of the ramp
Within 10 feet of the ramp
questions.explanation: You may not park within 3 feet of a sidewalk ramp used by people with disabilities.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking (Where It Is Illegal to Park)

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Move Over, Slow Down' law?
choices: To protect emergency responders, tow operators, and road workers stopped on the roadside
To speed up traffic flow near work zones
To allow emergency vehicles to park anywhere
To require drivers to stop completely at all roadside vehicles
questions.explanation: The law protects people working at the roadside by requiring drivers to move over a lane or slow down when passing stopped emergency, tow, or Caltrans vehicles.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Move Over, Slow Down Law

questions.question: How far ahead of a freeway lane change should you typically signal compared to a normal street turn?
choices: Signal earlier, about five seconds before changing lanes
Signal later, only as you begin moving over
Signaling is not required on freeways
Signal the same 100 feet as a street turn
questions.explanation: Because of higher speeds, you should signal about five seconds before a freeway lane change to give other drivers ample warning.

questions.question: When preparing to exit a freeway, when should you slow down?
choices: After you have moved into the deceleration lane or exit ramp
While still in the through lane, well before the exit
Only after you have fully left the freeway
You should never slow down on a freeway exit
questions.explanation: Stay at freeway speed until you enter the deceleration lane or exit ramp, then slow down so you do not impede traffic still on the freeway.

questions.question: If a pedestrian is walking slowly across the street with the help of a cane or walker, you should:
choices: Be patient and allow extra time for them to cross
Drive around them immediately
Honk to encourage them to move faster
Edge forward to pressure them along
questions.explanation: Older or disabled pedestrians may need more time to cross; be patient and let them complete their crossing safely.

questions.question: When a school crossing guard steps into the roadway holding a stop sign, you must:
choices: Stop and remain stopped until the guard signals you to go
Slow down but keep moving
Proceed if no children are visible
Drive around the guard carefully
questions.explanation: You must obey a school crossing guard's directions and stay stopped until the guard signals it is safe to proceed.

questions.question: When should you begin slowing down for a sharp curve?
choices: Before you enter the curve, so you are not braking hard while turning
Only after you feel the car begin to slide
In the middle of the curve to maintain momentum
You should accelerate through the entire curve
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve; braking hard while turning can cause a skid. Posted curve advisory speeds tell you a safe entry speed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — California's Basic Speed Law

questions.question: Which of the following will help a person sober up faster after drinking alcohol?
choices: Nothing — only the passage of time
Drinking strong coffee
Eating a large meal
Taking a cold shower
questions.explanation: Coffee, food, exercise, and cold showers do not speed up the elimination of alcohol. Only time allows the body to remove it.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: What is a center two-way left-turn lane (marked by solid and broken yellow lines) used for?
choices: Making left turns or U-turns, used by traffic from both directions
Passing slower vehicles in your direction of travel
Driving straight through during heavy traffic
Parking temporarily while waiting to turn
questions.explanation: A center two-way left-turn lane is shared by traffic in both directions and may only be used to prepare for and make left turns or U-turns, not for through travel or passing.

questions.question: If you must make or take an important phone call while driving and cannot use hands-free, you should:
choices: Pull over safely and stop before using the phone
Hold the phone low so it is less noticeable
Make the call quickly while driving slowly
Wait for a red light to make the call
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to pull over to a safe location and stop before using a hand-held phone, rather than driving distracted.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an all-way stop at the same time, side by side. Who should go first?
choices: The driver on the right goes first
The driver on the left goes first
The faster vehicle goes first
The larger vehicle goes first
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an all-way stop at the same time, the driver on the right has the right of way.

questions.question: Does the Minimum Speed Law mean you may drive as slowly as you like in the right lane?
choices: No; you may not drive so slowly that you block the normal, reasonable movement of traffic
Yes; there is no minimum speed anywhere in California
Yes, as long as you stay in the slow lane
Yes, but only on surface streets
questions.explanation: California law prohibits driving so slowly that you impede the normal and reasonable flow of traffic, unless reduced speed is necessary for safety.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving Too Slowly

questions.question: Under California's implied consent law, if you are lawfully arrested for DUI and refuse chemical testing, you will:
choices: Face license suspension or revocation plus added penalties
Receive only a verbal warning
Have the charges automatically dropped
Be allowed to retest later with no consequence
questions.explanation: Holding a California license means you consent to chemical testing if lawfully arrested for DUI. Refusing leads to a longer license suspension or revocation and additional penalties.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: At a stop sign where your view of cross traffic is blocked, what is the proper procedure?
choices: Stop, then edge forward slowly until you can see, yielding to cross traffic
Stop once at the line and then proceed regardless of what you can see
Roll through slowly if no cars are immediately visible
Speed up to clear the intersection before cross traffic arrives
questions.explanation: After stopping at the limit line, if your view is blocked you should inch forward until you can see, yielding to any cross traffic before proceeding.

questions.question: You realize you have just missed your freeway exit. What is the correct thing to do?
choices: Continue to the next exit and find another route back
Stop and back up on the shoulder to reach the exit
Make a U-turn through the median
Cross the gore point lines to reach the exit ramp
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, never stop or back up; continue to the next exit and find your way back from there.

questions.question: Why should you keep a space cushion all around your vehicle?
choices: It gives you room and time to react and avoid a collision
It allows you to drive faster than surrounding traffic
It is required only on the freeway
It lets you change lanes without signaling
questions.explanation: A space cushion on all sides gives you time and room to maneuver or stop if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped orange sign with a person holding a flag means what?
choices: A flagger is controlling traffic in a work zone ahead
A parade or special event is in progress
A crossing guard is on duty at a school
A surveying crew is measuring the road
questions.explanation: Orange is the color of work zones; the flagger-ahead sign means a person will direct traffic, and you must obey their signals.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Construction and Maintenance Signs

questions.question: On average, about how long does the body take to eliminate the alcohol from a single standard drink?
choices: About one hour
About 10 minutes
About three hours
It depends only on body weight
questions.explanation: The liver removes alcohol at a roughly fixed rate of about one drink per hour, and nothing can speed up that process.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving
